args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it, and find out why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an error rate of about 18%. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate has dropped to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The SEV2 for checkout-api is open and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result after it. It also lists two follow-ups: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before deploying it again, and find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed in staging.

No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
